Wenjie,

Would you be able to paste the code into an e-mail? It’s tough to diagnose otherwise.

One possibility is that the function being called is part of a list, e.g., a$func().

It might also help to use some of the other various tools that parse R profiling files, which sometimes give a clearer picture of what’s going on. There are several packages, including profr, proftools, and aprof, but I am partial to my own proftable() function:

library(devtools)
install_github('noamross/noamtools')
library(noamtools)

Rprof('out.prof')
SOME CODE
Rprof(NULL)

proftable('out.prof')

Noam

​

Sorry, noamtools had an unnecessary dependency on viridis, which I’ve removed. I think it should work if you install it now.

I profiled your code like so

Rprof("out.prof")
all.process(M = 2, n = 1000, mean = 0, sd = 1, m = 2, lambda = lambda, len = 100, ind.true = ind.true, x = x)
Rprof(NULL)
noamtools::proftable('out.prof')

Which returned this:

 PctTime Call                                                       
 57.9722 outer > FUN > <Anonymous>                                  
 39.9073 mybootstrap > mygaussian.multi > <Anonymous>               
  0.6257 mybootstrap > my.rgaussian > runif                         
  0.5678 mybootstrap > my.rgaussian > mygaussian.multi > <Anonymous>
  0.1854 mygaussian.multi > <Anonymous>                             
  0.1390 outer                                                      
  0.1275 mybootstrap > my.rgaussian                                 
  0.0811 mybootstrap > which                                        
  0.0579 mybootstrap > &                                            
  0.0579 mybootstrap > mygaussian.multi                             

Parent Call: all.process > ...

Total Time: 172.6 seconds
Percent of run time represented: 99.7 %

It looks like you have 2 anonymous calls taking up most of the time. The first is the function assigned as the FUN argument in outer, which is your mygaussian.multi(), the second is the mygaussian.multi() call in mybootstrap().

I note that these are custom functions created using inline. I’m not 100% sure how inline structures these functions but this is probably the reason you are getting anonymous calls. mygaussian.multi() is a wrapper for the compiled C function, which is itself anonymous.

R profiling won’t give you information on what’s going on inside a C function. For that you’ll need a different set of tools. On a mac, you can use the “Instruments” time profiler, which is part of Xcode. Not sure about other operating systems.

It looks like you have 2 anonymous calls taking up most of the time. The first is the function assigned as the FUN argument in outer, which is your mygaussian.multi(), the second is the mygaussian.multi() call in mybootstrap().

I note that these are custom functions created using inline. I’m not 100% sure how inline structures these functions but this is probably the reason you are getting anonymous calls. mygaussian.multi() is a wrapper for the compiled C function, which is itself anonymous.

R profiling won’t give you information on what’s going on inside a C function. For that you’ll need a different set of tools. On a mac, you can use the “Instruments” time profiler, which is part of Xcode. Not sure about other operating systems.
